collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Researchers want to record every tradition and place: record what families allow, or keep some things only spoken.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) wants to record every tradition on bark and mark every important place on a map, so nothing is ever lost. (friend) says some places and some songs are private: if they are written down, anyone can find them. What should the researchers do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) asks each family. Some places go on the map; some are marked only as a small circle meaning private. The record has holes in it. The holes are on purpose.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) records only the public things. The rest stays in memory, passed mouth to ear. (friend) teaches (subject) one of the private songs, just one, to keep in (subject.his/her) head and never write down.
